title: The best of all ways
hookLine: the highest dharma is to repeat the Name and do pure deeds (Sukhmani 3)

lines: A LIST OF NO, THEN A LIST OF YES.
A LADDER: OF ALL..., THIS ONE.
cards: After a long list of what doesn't measure up, a reader wants to know: so what does? Yesterday's stanzas set fasting, pilgrimage, ritual and learning beside the Name, one by one.
Stop there, and the third ashtpadi looks like a list of no. But it ends with a list of yes.
The last stanza is a ladder of superlatives: of all the ways, this one; of all the efforts, this one; of all the places, this one. And its first rung holds two things together.

teach.h: SARAB DHARAM: OF ALL WAYS OF LIVING.
teach.b: It begins: sarab dharam meh sresht dharam, har ko naam jap nirmal karam. Sarab: all. Dharam: a way of right living, a duty, a practice.
Sresht: highest, best. So: of all ways of right living, the highest is to chant the Name of God and do pure deeds.
Nirmal means spotless; karam means action. Here dharam is read not as a religion, an institution, but as duty, the way a person ought to live. So the line isn't a contest between faiths.
It's a statement about what a good life is made of: remembering, and clean action, held together. Then the ladder climbs, in paraphrase.
Of all rites, the highest is the company of the holy, which washes away evil thinking. Of all efforts, the best is to chant the Name of God, always.
Of all speech, the nectar is to hear God's praise and speak it with your tongue.
Of all places, the highest is the heart in which the Name of God dwells. Notice where the ladder ends. Not in a temple, not on a mountain: in a heart.
After yesterday's pilgrimages, the best place turns out to be the one you carry around.
And notice what's paired with the Name at the very top: nirmal karam, pure deeds. Remembering alone isn't the whole of it. It has to show up in what you do.

how: Sikhs reading Sukhmani recite this stanza at the end of the third ashtpadi; its opening line pairs the Name with pure deeds.

o: a temple's rule book for its priests
right living, the way a person ought to live
a single faith, set above all the others

games.q: the ladder of the last stanza — tap the pairs.
p: a heart where the Name dwells

s: dharam in this line means one religion versus others
here it is read as right living, duty, the way one ought to live.
nirmal karam means spotless, pure action
the line pairs it with chanting the Name.
the stanza names a holy city as the highest place
the highest place is the heart in which the Name dwells.

games.q: after a long list of efforts that don't equal the Name, the third ashtpadi names the highest way. what is it?
o: chanting the Name and doing pure deeds.
games.why: sarab dharam meh sresht dharam, har ko naam jap nirmal karam: the Name and spotless action, together.

practice: Pure here means clean: no angle, no audience, no score kept. Let one such deed come to mind, a compliment you mean, something borrowed and returned, litter no one will thank you for, and picture doing it simply.
If you pray, say Waheguru once, letting the Name and the deed sit side by side.

wordCard.voice: Dharam, right living: the last stanza of Sukhmani's third ashtpadi says, of all ways of right living, the highest is to chant the Name and do pure deeds, and the highest place is a heart where the Name lives.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: dharam, right living, duty; the line names the highest dharam.

carryVoice: Your line: name and pure deeds. No angle, no audience, no score kept. A week, gathered.

sources.ref: Gauri Sukhmani M5, ashtpadi 3, pauri 8, Ang 266
